SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #20 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice do Kenyan laws forbid because it harms girls? (1 mark)
   A. Wearing beads
   B. Female genital mutilation
   C. Cooking ugali
   D. Playing bao

2. In traditional culture, what do we call a basket or clay pot made and used by people? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of food
   B. An artefact
   C. A type of weather
   D. A river

3. Which is a good manner when interviewing an elder about culture? (1 mark)
   A. Laughing
   B. Greeting politely and asking permission to record
   C. Interrupting
   D. Refusing to listen

4. Which is a good school rule? (1 mark)
   A. Break desks
   B. Fight in class
   C. Write on walls
   D. Come to school on time

5. What is a gallery walk? (1 mark)
   A. A cooking lesson
   B. A race
   C. Walking round to look at displayed work
   D. A kind of assembly

6. What is mining? (1 mark)
   A. Growing maize
   B. Catching fish
   C. Cutting hair
   D. Taking minerals from the ground

7. Which county is famous for its tea farms? (1 mark)
   A. Marsabit
   B. Turkana
   C. Kericho
   D. Lamu

8. Where is soda ash taken from in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Lake Victoria
   B. Kisumu Port
   C. Mount Kenya
   D. Lake Magadi

9. What raw material is used in a cement factory? (1 mark)
   A. Sugarcane
   B. Limestone
   C. Milk
   D. Fish

10. Which of these is a jua kali product? (1 mark)
   A. A satellite
   B. A big ship
   C. A metal door made in a small workshop
   D. A jet plane

11. What should you do when visiting a factory? (1 mark)
   A. Stay with the group and not touch machines
   B. Touch all machines
   C. Shout
   D. Run around

12. Which of these can be a school enterprise project? (1 mark)
   A. A vegetable garden
   B. A war
   C. Bullying
   D. A robbery

13. Who should handle sharp tools in a school project? (1 mark)
   A. An adult
   B. Nobody
   C. A young child alone
   D. A visitor

14. Which of these is an honest practice in business? (1 mark)
   A. Cheating customers
   B. Selling bad goods as good
   C. Giving correct change
   D. Hiding sales money

15. Which action shows cooperation? (1 mark)
   A. Fighting
   B. Copying others
   C. Doing nothing
   D. Sharing tasks in a group

16. You find a lost pencil that belongs to a classmate. What should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Keep it
   B. Hide it
   C. Sell it
   D. Return it to the owner

17. Being good even when nobody is watching is called what? (1 mark)
   A. Integrity
   B. Boasting
   C. Fashion
   D. Punishment

18. What does fairness mean? (1 mark)
   A. Favouring rich people
   B. Treating everyone equally
   C. Favouring friends
   D. Ignoring people

19. What is bullying? (1 mark)
   A. Helping a friend
   B. Sharing food
   C. Playing together
   D. Repeatedly hurting or frightening someone weaker

20. What is a peace corner? (1 mark)
   A. A shop
   B. A place to hide
   C. A quiet place to calm down or talk through a problem
   D. A place to fight

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Write a short motto for a school and say what it means. (3 marks)

22. Plan a class culture day. State five things you would include. (5 marks)

23. Describe how to stay safe during a visit to a factory. Give four rules. (4 marks)

24. Explain what peace means in a school. (2 marks)

25. Describe how you would prepare a poster on the school values. (4 marks)

26. Name two artefacts made by communities in Kenya. (2 marks)

27. Explain why we should be honest even when nobody is watching. (3 marks)

28. Explain how you can stay calm when you feel very angry. (3 marks)

29. Explain what a raw material is and give one example. (2 marks)

30. Name two duties of a pupil in school. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #20 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Female genital mutilation
   FGM is against the law.

2. B — An artefact
   Baskets and pots are artefacts.

3. B — Greeting politely and asking permission to record
   Politeness shows respect.

4. D — Come to school on time
   Being punctual is a good habit.

5. C — Walking round to look at displayed work
   In a gallery walk pupils look at each other's displays.

6. D — Taking minerals from the ground
   Mining takes minerals such as soda ash or titanium from the earth.

7. C — Kericho
   Kericho is a major tea growing area.

8. D — Lake Magadi
   Soda ash is mined at Lake Magadi.

9. B — Limestone
   Cement is made using limestone.

10. C — A metal door made in a small workshop
   Jua kali workers make goods like doors and furniture.

11. A — Stay with the group and not touch machines
   Safety rules protect visitors.

12. A — A vegetable garden
   A garden can be run safely by pupils.

13. A — An adult
   Adults must handle dangerous tools.

14. C — Giving correct change
   Honesty is right in business.

15. D — Sharing tasks in a group
   Cooperation is working well with others.

16. D — Return it to the owner
   Returning shows honesty.

17. A — Integrity
   Integrity means doing right when unseen.

18. B — Treating everyone equally
   Fair people give everyone equal treatment.

19. D — Repeatedly hurting or frightening someone weaker
   Bullying is repeated unkind behaviour.

20. C — A quiet place to calm down or talk through a problem
   A peace corner helps pupils settle problems.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Work hard, be kind. It means pupils should study well and be kind to others.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a short motto, 1 mark for its meaning, 1 mark for showing action.

22. (5 marks)
   Answer: Traditional dress, foods to taste, songs and dances, artefacts on display, and stories told by elders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct item.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Stay with the group, do not touch machines, listen to the guide, and wear safety clothing if given.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: Peace means pupils and teachers live together safely, respect each other and settle disagreements without fighting.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for safety and respect, 1 mark for solving conflict peacefully.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose the values, write a large title, draw a picture for each value, and use bright colours that can be seen from far.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: A kiondo basket and a soapstone carving. Accept clay pots, beaded jewellery or wooden stools.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each artefact.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Honesty builds trust, it is right, and it prepares us to be good citizens.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Walk away, take slow deep breaths, and count to ten before speaking.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: A raw material is a material used to make something new, for example sugarcane used to make sugar.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for example.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: Follow the school rules and respect others. Accept care for property or do class duties.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each duty.
